summary.intent: Plan and execute CipherBox Phase 69 (FUSE and WinFsp Rust integration with grant-root awareness) end-to-end using the GSD plan-phase and execute-phase orchestration workflows.
summary.outcome: Planning produced 18 plans; execution merged 16/18 with a green workspace after three successive architectural blockers forced expanding the phase (write-plane emit API, write-owner materialization, and legacy-type retirement) to be built and landed via a bounded multi-slice grind. 69-14 (WinFsp) is deferred to the user's Windows machine, and 69-10 (delete legacy types) is blocked pending two new plans (69-19 bin, 69-20 vault-creation) being authored when the transcript ends.

repo: GSD commit helper frequently reports 'commit_failed' even when the commit landed cleanly (lint-staged false negative) — always verify via `git log --oneline -1`, never retry the commit.

gsd-executor agents sometimes mis-report `expected_base` as their own last docs commit rather than the true worktree fork point — verify via `git merge-base worktree-agent-<id> HEAD` before recording/merging.
cargo fmt run at the crate root can reformat unrelated files; executors must scope-check diffs and revert out-of-scope reformatting before committing.

ApiNodeFetcher is a borrow adapter with no `::new` constructor — must be constructed inline at each read-path call site, not stored as a struct field (would be self-referential with an owned Arc<ApiClient>).
RotationHighWater<S> was not Clone by default; adding #[derive(Clone)] was safe since its JsonSidecarFloorStore only holds a PathBuf doing read-modify-write on disk.
D-07 dual-keying convention: SealedChildRef is keyed by ipnsName (read plane), WriteChildRef is keyed by childId UUID (write plane) — must never conflate the two.
Terminal-owner zeroization is enforced by the type system: parent_read_key/parent_write_key are passed as borrows (&[u8]), so a function physically cannot zero the caller's buffer.
The desktop CI workflow is actually named 'Desktop E2E Tests', not 'CI E2E Tests' as ROADMAP/CONTEXT docs stated — `gh workflow run` with the wrong name would 404.

crates/fuse's Windows platform code is feature-gated (`default=["fuse"]`, `cfg(feature="winfsp")`) and excluded from default `cargo check --workspace` — only verified under `--features winfsp` in a separate CI lane.

Legacy types (FolderMetadata, FilePointer, FolderEntry) remain load-bearing for the recycle-bin, vault-export, and vault-creation subsystems that Phase 69's node/v3 migration deliberately did not touch — a 'delete all legacy types' plan premise can be stale.

A research/plan's cited cross-crate 'weld' (JournalOp.parent_metadata: FolderMetadata in queue.rs) turned out to be nonexistent/stale against the live tree — always re-grep-verify plan acceptance criteria against current code before executing, especially after delay.

Desktop root read/write key recovery into KeyState is an unwired phase-63-class stub (same as the web v2.0 client) — desktop can't mount a real node/v3 vault until that recovery is built, making desktop-e2e structurally unreachable as a merge gate.

code.finding: ResolvedChild carries no key material; resolve_child unseals a child's read key and immediately zeroizes it (D-09), never touching the write-body — read-only listing clients can't recover write-plane keys.

InodeKind::{Root,Folder,File} is a full read-write vault-owner state (stores ipns_private_key + folder/file keys) since the FUSE mount signs IPNS records and seals new children, unlike the read-only web 68.2 mirror.
JournalOp has no parent_metadata: FolderMetadata field as originally cited by research — only hex-string fields (wrapped_key_hex, parent_ipns_key_hex, etc.); the reshape target for 69-18.
Desktop bridges read_key/write_key from the legacy root_folder_key as a placeholder because real node/v3 root-key recovery into KeyState isn't wired yet.

workflow: When a subagent halts with an architectural blocker instead of forcing broken code, independently re-verify its grep/evidence claims against the live tree before accepting or escalating to the user — subagents can be both overcautious and, separately, exactly right.

For an unmergeable atomic multi-thousand-line change, chunk it into bounded 'slices' executed serially on the same worktree branch, each committing independently even while RED, with a committed runbook recording the authoritative target shape and carry-forward facts between slices so the grind survives usage-limit interruptions.

Prefer gating a large, hard-to-unit-test crypto/FS migration's final merge on a real E2E run rather than compile-green alone, once project memory shows compile-clean crypto has previously shipped runtime-broken.
Canary the very first plan of a wave synchronously (not in parallel) to validate the full executor→worktree→merge→build pipeline before fanning out the rest in parallel.
Use a durable scratchpad handoff file, updated after every major step, so full recovery state survives pauses, /compact, and session/context resets.

friction: gsd-planner crashed mid-run twice due to API errors (once during initial planning after writing 13/14 plans, once during an executor run), requiring filesystem-fallback recovery each time.
Executor agents stalled/failed mid-stream from API errors independent of any code issue (one hit the account session limit entirely, resetting at a fixed time).

Three successive, only-discovered-during-execution architectural gaps (missing write-plane emit API, missing write-owner tree materialization, invalid 'delete all legacy types' premise) despite an upfront research and planning pass — each required pausing execution, researching, re-planning, and getting explicit user approval before continuing.
The GSD commit helper's false-negative ('commit_failed' on a commit that actually succeeded) recurred on nearly every commit throughout the session, requiring manual git log verification each time.
cargo fmt run against the crate root repeatedly reformatted unrelated files, requiring manual scope-checking and reverting before every commit.
Session context needed a /compact partway through the long execution phase.

The atomic FUSE cutover plan (69-09) itself proved far larger than estimated at each new sub-scope (Slice 5 alone ballooned from an estimated 'mechanical field-repointing' pass into ~250 legacy test-compile errors plus a full refresh-pipeline redesign).
open_items: 69-10 (delete legacy core types) is blocked — its D-04 clean-delete premise is invalid since recycle-bin, vault-export, and vault-creation subsystems still depend on legacy types; needs re-scoping after 69-19/69-20 land.
69-19 (recycle-bin node/v3 migration) and 69-20 (vault-creation node/v3 migration) were being authored by a planner when the transcript ends — not yet reviewed, plan-checked, or executed.
crates/core/src/decrypt.rs identified as dead code (no live consumers) and slated for deletion alongside 69-10.
69-14 (WinFsp/Windows integration, TEST-03/SC#5) is explicitly deferred (`autonomous: false`) to the user's own Windows machine.
Desktop root-key recovery into KeyState is an unwired stub — real desktop-e2e validation of the node/v3 FUSE cutover remains impossible until that separate runtime-integration effort lands.

ROT-06/ROT-07 gap: no production RotationDeps implementor exists anywhere in the workspace, so shared-scope-exit deletes/moves on Unix currently return EIO until the rotation engine is live-wired (private deletes are unaffected).
File `versions` are not reconstructed on write since InodeKind dropped the versions field in the flip — flagged as a versioning regression to verify once E2E is runnable.
file_iv hex round-trip (write encodes hex, content_ops decodes hex) flagged for E2E verification rather than fully proven.
Orphaned parent-CID pins are no longer unpinned on republish (metadata_cache no longer surfaces the old CID) — GC-able but not yet addressed.
SC#6 CI grep gate allowlist covers only the recycle-bin and reencrypt raw-resolve sites in metadata.rs; should be re-examined once 69-19/69-20 change that code.
